html:
The Wonnarua are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Upper Hunter Valley in New South Wales. They lived in family groups and clans along the valley, united by strong ties of kinship. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their creation spirit is Baiame, also called Koin, the creator of all things and the Keeper of the Valley. The Hunter River and its creeks gave fish and eels, and the valley's open woodland held kangaroo and other game.

After a convict settlement was set up at the river mouth at Newcastle in 1804, settlers spread up the valley in the 1820s with land grants for grazing, and conflict followed. The Hunter later became known for wine and coal. Neighbours on the map include the Darkinyung, the Awabakal, the Worimi and the Kamilaroi. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
